## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

This one-fascicle text by [吉迦夜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%BF%A6%E5%A4%9C) Kiṅkara (Jíjiāyè 吉迦夜, active c. 472 CE in Northern Wèi Píngchéng 平城 / modern Dàtóng) is a Northern-Wèi-period Chinese rendering of *Daśabhūmika*-related material. Distinct from the major translations of the *Daśabhūmika-sūtra* — [Zhú Fǎhù's T0285](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0033), [Kumārajīva's T0286](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0034), and [Śīladharma's T0287](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6e/KR6e0035) — the present text appears to be a shorter independent recension of the same essential doctrinal material.

**Abstract**

The translation is precisely datable to *Yánxìng* 延興 2 (472 CE) per the *Chū sānzàng jì jí* 出三藏記集 ([KR6s0084](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6s/KR6s0084), juan 9) and the *Lìdài sānbǎo jì* 歷代三寶紀 ([KR6r0011](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0011), juan 9), when [吉迦夜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%90%89%E8%BF%A6%E5%A4%9C) Kiṅkara worked at Píngchéng under the patronage of the Northern Wèi Xiànwéndì 顯文帝 (later Xiàowéndì 孝文帝, who ascended in 471) with the assistance of the lay scholar [曇曜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E6%9B%9C) Tányào. The bracket adopted here (472 – 472) reflects this precise date.

Kiṅkara is associated primarily with the *Záyù běnshēng jīng* 雜寶藏經 ([KR6b0060](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0060)) and the *Dà fāngguǎng pútísà shí dì jīng* (the present text); his collaborator [曇曜](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9B%87%E6%9B%9C) Tányào was the abbot of the Yúngāng 雲岡 monastery and the guiding force behind the great Yúngāng cave-temple complex commissioned by the Northern-Wèi imperial house. The doctrinal substance of the present text — the bodhisattva's ten-stage path — places it in the *Daśabhūmika* tradition, but the Chinese rendering is brief enough (1 fascicle, versus T0285's 5 fascicles, T0286's 4 fascicles, T0287's 9 fascicles) that it must represent a substantially compressed Indic original or a deliberate Chinese epitome.

The Taishō text (T0308) is established on the standard apparatus.
